title: IRS reminder: Information return e-file system transitioning to a new platform | Internal Revenue Service
text: Skip to main content IRS reminder: Information return e-file system transitioning to a new platform English Español 中文 (简体) More In News Working Families Tax Cuts News releases News releases for frequently asked questions Tax relief in disaster situations Topics in the news Fact sheets IRS statements and announcements IRS Tax Tips IRS guidance Multimedia center Tax articles to share Posters to share IR-2026-99, Aug. 24, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Internal Revenue Service today reminded information return filers who currently use the Filing Information Returns Electronically (FIRE) system to prepare now for the system’s retirement and transition to the Information Returns Intake System (IRIS) before the 2027 filing season. After the November maintenance window, filers will no longer be able to submit information returns through FIRE. Current FIRE users must transition to IRIS to file tax year 2026 information returns during the 2027 filing season. Key dates to remember Nov. 1, 2026: Last day to file test information returns through the FIRE Trading Partner Test System. Nov. 9, 2026: Last day to make changes to the Information Returns (IR) Applications for Transmitter Control Codes (TCC). Nov. 19, 2026, at 3 p.m. ET: Last day to file information returns through the FIRE system. Transitioning to IRIS IRIS is a modernized system that receives information returns through two channels: the IRIS Taxpayer Portal and IRIS Application to Application. IRIS became available in 2023 as part of a phased transition of forms from FIRE. Beginning in 2027, all forms previously supported by FIRE will be available through IRIS. The IRIS Taxpayer Portal is a free, web-based filing system that allows filers to e-file up to 100 returns at a time. Filers can enter information manually or upload it using a CSV file. They can also download payee copies and maintain records of completed and filed forms. Filers who use third-party software or develop their own software can use IRIS Application to Application to e-file larger volumes of information returns. To prepare for the transition, filers should: Complete an IRIS Application for TCC. Review available guidance on E-file Information Returns with IRIS. Subscribe to IRIS QuickAlerts for updates about system changes, maintenance, and working group meetings. Register for IRIS Working Group meetings and review meeting materials. IRIS Working Group meetings are held on the second Wednesday of each month. Participants must register each month to receive the meeting link. Meeting notifications are sent to IRIS QuickAlerts subscribers. The IRS will provide additional information through IRIS QuickAlerts, IRIS Working Group meetings, and IRS.gov. For more information, see Filing Information Returns Electronically (FIRE) and E-file Information Returns with IRIS on IRS.gov. News items may not be updated after their release.
